title: The Fox and the Folk

full_text:
A cunning old fox lived in a rocky den overlooking a prosperous agricultural village. For years, the fox raided the village hen-roosts by night, snatching fat pullets and ducks, while the angry farmers set iron traps, laid poisoned meat, and sent fierce hounds into the woods to hunt him down. The fox lived in constant anxiety, with bruised paws and frayed fur.

One freezing winter, when deep snow covered the valley, the village orchards were threatened by an army of field mice and voles that were gnawing the bark of the apple trees, threatening to destroy the entire harvest.

The old fox observed the disaster and devised a treaty of peace. He sat upon a stone wall near the village gate, outside the reach of the dogs, and called out to the village elder:

'O farmers! Why do we live in endless war? You hunt me with hounds, and I snatch your chickens in hunger. Let us establish a treaty of friendship: appoint me the guardian of your orchards! I will hunt down every mouse and vole in your fields, protecting your apple trees; and in return, you shall place a bowl of fresh milk and scraps of bread for me beside the mill every evening!'

The farmers, desperate to save their trees, accepted the bargain.

The fox kept his word faithfully: within two weeks, his sharp teeth had cleared the orchards of every rodent. The farmers, in gratitude, kept the wooden bowl filled with sweet milk and bread every night.

The hounds slept peacefully, the chickens roosted without fear, and the old fox grew sleek and content, having learned that peaceful cooperation is a thousand times more rewarding than the perilous life of a thief.
moral: Peaceful cooperation and respecting boundaries are far safer than endless predatory raids.
